title: Start SOC 2 Type I
summary: Begin SOC 2 Type I compliance journey using Vanta, set up policies, and begin evidence collection.

parts.title: Create an account with your compliance platform
parts.guidance: Identify the assurance report customers have requested and the service it must cover. Compare platforms on integrations with your infrastructure, evidence export, access controls and compatibility with the prospective auditor’s process. Separate subscription, implementation and examination fees. Complete the approved purchase, then create a company-owned workspace with a named administrator and the chosen framework.

options.title: Default — Create an account with your compliance platform
options.summary: Use this route for a SOC 2 examination of the selected service. Set up the compliance workspace under company ownership, identify who will run the compliance program and verify the features included in the purchased plan. Use the prospective auditor’s scope to choose integrations and evidence work. The software account supports preparation; the separate audit engagement determines what will be examined.

options.title: UK - Cyber Essentials first
options.summary: Obtain the UK customer or tender’s exact requirement, including whether it specifies Cyber Essentials or Cyber Essentials Plus. Use the current NCSC materials to scope the assessment and identify gaps in the technical controls. Choose the certification route and identify its required assessment signatory. Follow a separate Cyber Essentials assessment plan; the later SOC 2 examination steps are not its certification procedure.
options.when: Selling to UK buyers - the asked-for framework differs

options.title: Germany - ISO 27001 first
options.summary: Ask the German customer for its required certification scope and whether it specifically names IT-Grundschutz. Compare that requirement with the company’s information-security management system and prospective certifier’s process. BSI describes an ISO 27001 route based on IT-Grundschutz with its own examination and certification requirements. Map the chosen route to a separate work plan; the following SOC 2 steps do not supply that certification.
options.when: Selling to German enterprise - the asked-for framework differs

options.title: France - ISO 27001 / SecNumCloud
options.summary: Identify the assurance required by the French customer for the particular service. If it specifies SecNumCloud, examine the ANSSI qualification scope and distinguish your offering from an underlying provider’s qualified cloud service. Record ISO 27001 requirements separately if requested. Build the chosen qualification or certification plan; selecting this option does not convert the following SOC 2 steps into a French qualification workflow.
options.when: Selling to French buyers - the asked-for framework differs

parts.title: Connect integrations
parts.guidance: Connect the cloud accounts, repositories, identity systems and device inventories inside the proposed audit boundary. Check requested permissions and obtain each system owner’s authorization before granting access. Verify that collection covers the intended accounts and environments, including assets missing from the first import. An empty or stale result needs investigation before it can support a control assessment.

verify.how: The compliance platform's automated monitoring tests start reporting against each connected system.

parts.title: Generate security policies
parts.guidance: Draft policies from the company’s actual security procedures and architecture. Name who handles access, incidents, releases and other subjects in the agreed control scope, and link to instructions staff can follow. Distinguish current practice from proposed improvements. Leave unresolved operational choices visible for the people who run those systems to answer before the policies are adopted.

parts.title: Review and customize policies
parts.guidance: Walk each policy through a realistic new hire, access change, release or incident with the people who would use it. Resolve conflicts with actual tooling, customer commitments and existing agreements. If a promised practice does not exist, revise the policy or assign its implementation. The relevant business and security owners approve the effective version, which staff should be able to find and understand.

parts.title: Configure automated tests
parts.guidance: For each automated check, identify the control objective, assets covered, expected result and person responsible for failures. Test against a known configuration and verify that stale or missing collection triggers attention. Decide which failures create remediation work and how exceptions are reviewed. Document the human evidence still needed where an automated check cannot demonstrate the whole control.

parts.title: Remediate failing tests
parts.guidance: Investigate failed checks in the underlying system. Distinguish actual control gaps from stale inventory, connector permissions and unsuitable test settings. Fix confirmed gaps through the normal change process, rerun the check and attach the resulting evidence to the issue. Record accepted exceptions with their rationale and reviewer, and link later passing results to the original failure and its remediation.

parts.title: Employee security training
parts.guidance: Teach staff the security practices they need for their access: handling customer information, reporting suspicious activity and getting help with account problems. Use examples from the company’s actual procedures. Use the agreed audience and invitation process, then track completion and follow up on missing participants. Questions that reveal unclear policy or unusable tools should become specific changes to the program.

parts.title: Engage auditor
parts.guidance: Discuss the requested report, system boundary, readiness gaps and evidence inventory with prospective auditors. Check qualifications, independence, scope, fees, evidence expectations and intended recipients. Ask how evidence collected by the compliance platform fits the examination. The company’s authorized representative signs the agreed engagement; control owners can then work from the auditor’s actual request list and scope.

parts.title: Complete audit
parts.guidance: Supply evidence for the auditor’s agreed scope and dates, explaining missing records and exceptions accurately. Management reviews the system description and representations before signing. Check the issued report for factual errors, agree its permitted distribution and assign follow-up for exceptions. Completion is an issued report with its scope and unresolved findings understood by management.

geoNotes.summary: UK buyers ask for Cyber Essentials (the NCSC-backed baseline, mandatory for many government contracts) and ISO 27001 more often than SOC 2 — SOC 2 still travels for US-facing sales.
German enterprise security reviews anchor on ISO 27001 (historically also 'auf Basis von BSI IT-Grundschutz') rather than SOC 2 — plan ISO 27001 if the pipeline is DACH enterprise.
French buyers look for ISO 27001, and cloud vendors selling to the public sector meet ANSSI's SecNumCloud qualification — SOC 2 is a US-market artifact here.

metadata.supportReason: Vanta API supports test monitoring and evidence collection. Policy creation and auditor engagement need human input.
